title: Opportunistic prefetch, token-shedding, and concurrent evaluation for reranking endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The reranking endpoint suffers from tail latency on mixed workloads (small single-candidate requests interleaved with large batch reranks). Our current batching approach increases throughput but contributes to high p95/p99 latency for latency-sensitive clients. Goal: Implement an opportunistic prefetch + token-shedding strategy with concurrent candidate evaluation that respects per-request latency budgets, reduces p95 by ~30% for high-priority requests, keeps throughput within 10% of baseline, and limits rerank quality regression to <0.5% MRR on our evaluation set. Scope: server-side routing, microbatch sizing, KV-prefetch heuristics, deadline-aware early exit, and new observability surfaces for per-request token usage and time budgets.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for priority=high rerank requests reduces by >=30% under mixed workload (measured on perf-lab cluster)
end-to-end throughput within 10% of current baseline in steady-state for heavy traffic patterns
Quality regression <= 0.5% MRR on standard rerank eval suite (stable across two independent runs)
No customer-facing errors introduced (error rate change <= +0.05 percentage points)
Feature gated behind runtime-1.26 toggle with rollout plan and metrics dashboard
decision_log: 2026-02-11: Decided to implement token-shedding (dynamic candidate truncation) rather than full candidate sampling to keep ranking determinism.
2026-02-15: Chosen opportunistic prefetch model: prefetch top-K candidate embeddings into KV cache for candidate-heavy requests and mark low-confidence candidates for lazy evaluation.
2026-02-20: Use deadline-aware concurrent evaluation using per-request time budget; requests hitting budget trigger earliest safe early-exit policy (stop after next boundary) rather than hard kill.
2026-02-24: Concurrency model will use work-stealing across microbatches to avoid GPU underutilization while preserving latency SLOs.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Spike, 1 week): Measure baseline instrumentation, simulate mixed workloads in perf-lab (small:100req/s, large:10req/s with 64 candidates).
Phase 2 (Core infra, 2sprint): Build KV-prefetch heuristics, token-shedding policy, and deadline-aware scheduler; add async concurrent evaluation path in runtime.
Phase 3 (Quality shield, 1sprint): Integrate rerank eval harness to run nightly comparisons and add regression alerting to Optimize pipeline.
Phase 4 (Canary rollout, 2 weeks): Gradual rollout by customer tier: 5% -> 20% -> 50% with automated rollback on latency/quality breaches.
Phase 5 (Post-rollout): Tune autoscaling and batching knobs, finalize docs and SDK flags, and add runbook entries.

testing_notes: Load tests: synthetic mixes - bursty small requests (1-4 candidates) + bulk rerank (64-128 candidates); run for 30 minutes per scenario.
Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency per priority, throughput (req/s), token consumption per request, GPU utilization, and MRR on eval suite.
A/B test: Route 20k daily live user rerank requests for 2 weeks to canary; compare conversion delta and quality metrics.
Chaos testing: Simulate KV cache misses and slow downstream storage to validate early-exit safety.
